reviewer: Claude coordinator and independent Claude review agents (text, illustrations)
text: Independent review agent read all six scenes, five vocabulary entries, the pause question, two discussion questions, alt texts, content note, provenance and adaptation changes in full against the full Ryder text, and re-read and approved the corrected text.

Blockers fixed before approval: the frame now correctly says Red-Eye tells the tale to the crow Live-Strong; the daughter herself asks to become a mouse again, as in the source; ದೊಡ್ಡವಳಾದಳು (a puberty euphemism) was replaced by ಬೆಳೆದು ಯುವತಿಯಾದಳು; the moral change is disclosed.

The source's moral, that one's nature is hard to change, was deliberately replaced by 'even a tiny mouse can wear down a mountain', so the story does not tell a child she must return to the kind she was born into.
The source's age of twelve is stated honestly in the parent note; the search happens after she grows up and she chooses her groom. The pause question precedes the mountain's answer. No em dashes.
illustrations: Panel 1: the mouse sits unhurt in the sage's cupped palms; the hawk flies away with empty beak and talons.
Panels 2 and 3: sun, clouds and wind are natural, with no faces; the daughter shades her eyes and laughs in the wind.
Panel 4: mice peek from burrows at the mountain's foot. Panel 6: two mice at the burrow and the sage's raised-palm blessing; no wedding ritual.

Panel 5 was edited once so the daughter clearly reads as a young woman of about twenty at the moment she chooses; the edited panel was composited at x=0, y=1024 with no visible join. Only her small bindi dropped out.
The sage wears a rudraksha mala and a forehead mark but no sacred thread: religious markers that fit a sage, not caste markers. Both people are dignified and never caricatured.
Grid: seams at y=512/1024 and x=513 (1 px right, from the original generation, imperceptible). Accepted minor issues: storybook-large mice and a walking staff only in panel 4.
limitations: AI-agent editorial review, not human Kannada-teacher or scholar certification.
Age suitability has not been tested with children; apparent ages in the art are subjective readings.
Source fidelity was checked against the full rendered Wikisource text of Ryder's 1925 translation, not against Durgasimha's Kannada text or a Sanskrit recension.
Art was judged on the full sheet and 512px panel crops with pixel measurement of the grid; not every scene was checked in the app's dark mode.
